title: Atomic cost-latency view — UX hypotheses & wireframe drafts
notes:
Purpose and context:
We need a compact, interactive surface that explains per-request economics at the smallest meaningful unit — an 'atomic' view that lets engineers and platform owners quickly answer questions like:
- Which tokens (system/prompt/user/assistant) are driving my bill?
- Where is time being spent (tokenization, first-byte, model compute, KV fetch)?
- Which prompt edits or model variants would materially change cost or latency?

This doc captures UX hypotheses, two small wireframe drafts (text descriptions), a candidate backlog, and acceptance signals for an initial prototype (console + lightweight trace integration).

Audience / personas (primary):
- Platform engineer (SRE) investigating production latency regressions and cost spikes
- ML engineer optimizing prompt templates and batching strategies
- Product manager verifying economic impact of a new feature that increases average request length

Top-line hypotheses (to validate):
H1: Showing per-token cost + latency (with token grouping by role and semantic span) reduces time-to-root-cause for cost spikes by >30% vs current per-request view.
H2: An interactive slicer that lets users switch between 'byte', 'token', and 'semantic-span' grouping will make tradeoffs actionable for ML engineers (prompt edits -> cost delta preview).
H3: Exposing fast, approximate cost deltas for small prompt edits (local diff preview) increases the number of optimization changes applied by teams.

Key metrics to instrument:
- Median time to diagnose cost spike (baseline: current console request view)
- Number of 'preview edits' executed per team per week (engagement proxy)
- % of requests with KV cache hits (observability tie-in)
- Accuracy of previewed cost deltas (approx vs real)

Wireframe A (compact request row expansion) — description: 
- Table of requests (existing list). Each row can expand into an 'atomic breakdown' panel. Panel shows: compact header (model, route, tokens, cost, latency), then three horizontal bands: Role-slices (system/prompt/user), Token waterfall (stacked bar where each bar is a token group with hover showing cost/latency), and Operation timeline (tokenization -> first-byte -> model-step -> kv-io each as color segments).
- Interactions: hover a token group to highlight example tokens and show 'delta preview' button. Click delta opens a tiny editor overlay that shows estimated cost/latency after edit (quick approximation, 95% confidence).
- Benefit: minimal disruption to list UI. Great for spot checks and quick triage.

Wireframe B (exploration canvas) — description: 
- Full-screen canvas for deep dives. Left pane: request timeline with per-token markers (zoomable). Middle: token-level waterfall with a pinable token inspector showing raw token text (redacted options), estimated token-cost, compute-time, and KV-dependency indicator. Right pane: scenario panel — a place to run hypothetical changes (remove system tokens, compress prompt, switch model/quantization) and preview cost + latency deltas across 3 confidence bands (p50,p90,p99).
- Special: link a trace id to SLO dashboard and allow 'fallback simulation' (if model falls back to cheaper variant, show expected latencies).

Data model notes (practical):
- We can't show raw token text for PII-heavy requests by default. Add per-tenant redaction toggles and an explicit 'Reveal tokens' permission.
- Cost attribution: compute both on-the-wire token counts and estimated decode token expansion (some models expand; store mapping when available).
- Latency attribution: we need granular server-side timers (tokenize_start, kv_lookup_start, kv_lookup_end, decode_start, kernel_time). If not all present, fall back to approximations and mark as 'estimated'.

Interaction patterns and microcopy (quick wins):
- Hover: show cost/latency popover with exact numbers and link to raw trace.
- Pinning: allow engineers to pin a token group to persist inspector while browsing other requests.
- Delta preview microcopy: 'Estimated change to monthly spend if this edit shipped: $X (±Y%)'
- Permission microcopy: 'Tokens redacted — request Reveal Tokens permission to view content'

Backlog (prioritized):
- P0: Backend: expose per-request timing buckets and per-token role grouping (JIRA-IR-876).
- P0: Console: expandable request-row panel + hover popovers (prototype A).
- P1: Canvas: full-screen exploration canvas + simulated edits panel.
- P1: Delta preview engine: lightweight estimator service (fast, conservative).
- P2: Permissions: redaction ui and audit log links.
- P2: A/B: Evaluate showing cost delta precomputed vs computed-on-demand for perf/cost tradeoffs.

Acceptance criteria / success signals: 
- Prototype reduces median triage time in pilot org by 30%.
- Delta preview accuracy within 20% of real cost in 90% of sampled requests.
- No PII exposures in pilot (audit checks pass).

Open questions / risks: 
- How do we attribute cost for streaming responses where tokens are generated over time? (suggestion: show per-chunk incremental cost and cumulative).
- Tokenization differences across models complicate cross-model delta previews. Do we for now constrain preview to same tokenization family?
- Estimator drift: we must show confidence and surface 'last-calibrated' date.

Prototype plan & next 6 weeks: 
Week 1: Backend interface (timing buckets + minimal per-token metadata) — owner: Leo.
Week 2: Console proof-of-concept (expandable row, hover popover) — owner: Ava. Quick usability session with SREs.
Week 3-4: Delta preview + small estimator service + safety gating — owner: Maya.
Week 5: Canvas MVP + link-to-trace integration — owner: Dante.
Week 6: Pilot with 3 internal teams, collect triage time and qualitative feedback — owner: Ava/Maya.

Notes-to-self / loose ideas (brainstorm fragments):
- 'Slicer' control could be a brush over timeline to isolate token ranges and 'simulate compressing' that span.
- Consider a heatmap mode for long requests (>500 tokens) rather than per-token bars.
- Could compute per-role amortized cost per token to show 'system tokens tax' as a % of request spend.
- Lightweight 'cost-recommendations' engine: propose top 3 edits ranked by cost impact and expected risk to quality (score from evals).

Immediate asks for design review:
- Quick thumbs on compact panel vs canvas priority (we need to decide which to prototype first).
- Feedback on delta-preview risk messaging and UI placement.
